optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Capacity Planning Analyst, Wealth Services Platform

professionalSummary.text: Seasoned capacity planning professional with proven track record in forecasting month‑end batch demand, managing compute and storage resources, and driving significant reductions in batch overruns for a private bank’s wealth services platform.
professionalSummary.witness: Maintained the month‑end demand model that forecasts batch volume from client, account and report counts, refreshing the coefficients each quarter from the platform's job‑history tables.

experienceHighlights.text: Maintained and refreshed a demand model that accurately forecasts batch volume from client, account and report counts.
experienceHighlights.witness: Maintained the month‑end demand model that forecasts batch volume from client, account and report counts, refreshing the coefficients each quarter from the platform's job‑history tables.

experienceHighlights.text: Planned compute and storage capacity for each month‑end cycle, translating forecasts into node reservations and storage headroom.
experienceHighlights.witness: Planned compute and storage for each month‑end cycle with the platform team, translating the forecast into node reservations and storage headroom in the capacity plan.

experienceHighlights.text: Reduced month‑end batch overruns from 9 to 2 per cycle over six cycles, meeting the platform's published baseline.
experienceHighlights.witness: Month‑end batch overruns fell from 9 per cycle to 2 per cycle over the six cycles after the re‑sequenced valuation jobs went live, as recorded in the platform's overrun report against its published baseline of 9 overruns per cycle for the preceding half‑year.

experienceHighlights.text: Coordinated capacity changes with platform and finance teams, securing approvals and cost sign‑offs.
experienceHighlights.witness: Coordinated capacity changes with the platform and finance teams in the monthly capacity review; reservation changes were approved by the platform manager and the cost impact was signed off by finance.

experienceHighlights.text: Documented model assumptions, limitations, and hand‑over items for each planning cycle.
experienceHighlights.witness: Wrote the assumptions note for each planning cycle, listing the model coefficients, the known limitation that ad‑hoc adviser reports were outside the forecast and the hand‑over items for the next cycle.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Provided a work sample comprising the overrun report extract for six cycles and the assumptions note for one cycle, including export identifiers as a verification trail.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the overrun report extract for the six cycles (overruns per cycle, baseline line, go‑live marker for the re‑sequenced jobs) and the assumptions note for one cycle, with the report's export identifiers as a verification trail.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The resume and work sample provide direct evidence of the candidate’s responsibilities, outcomes, and documentation practices for the capacity planning role, but do not include independent third‑party verification beyond the referenced platform manager note.

decisionBoundary.statement: Candidate has evidence for all requirements but further verification is needed.

role.roleTitle: Capacity Planning Analyst, Wealth Services Platform

evidence.text: Maintained the month‑end demand model that forecasts batch volume from client, account and report counts, refreshing the coefficients each quarter from the platform's job‑history tables.
Planned compute and storage for each month‑end cycle with the platform team, translating the forecast into node reservations and storage headroom in the capacity plan.

Month‑end batch overruns fell from 9 per cycle to 2 per cycle over the six cycles after the re‑sequenced valuation jobs went live, as recorded in the platform's overrun report against its published baseline of 9 overruns per cycle for the preceding half‑year.

Coordinated capacity changes with the platform and finance teams in the monthly capacity review; reservation changes were approved by the platform manager and the cost impact was signed off by finance.

Wrote the assumptions note for each planning cycle, listing the model coefficients, the known limitation that ad‑hoc adviser reports were outside the forecast and the hand‑over items for the next cycle.

supportedClaims.claim: Month‑end batch overruns fell from 9 to 2 per cycle over six cycles.
supportedClaims.witness: Month‑end batch overruns fell from 9 per cycle to 2 per cycle over the six cycles after the re‑sequenced valuation jobs went live, as recorded in the platform's overrun report against its published baseline of 9 overruns per cycle for the preceding half‑year.

humanReviewChecklist: Verify overrun figures with platform manager via independent source
Confirm that capacity reservations were approved by finance and platform manager
Obtain third‑party audit of demand model accuracy
Ensure documentation of model assumptions is retained for future cycles
hiringEvidencePacket.auditSummary: The candidate’s resume and work sample provide comprehensive evidence that all listed requirements are met, with high‑confidence verifications for forecasting, capacity planning, overrun reduction, coordination, and documentation. However, the evidence is self‑reported and relies on internal notes; independent confirmation is recommended before a hiring decision.
limitations: Evidence limited to self‑reported resume and internal notes; external verification needed to confirm accuracy of overrun figures and approval records.
